links.reason: Not eating alone (அமிழ்தம் இயைவதாயினும் ... தமியர் உண்டலும் இலரே) and பகுத்துண்டு ... எல்லாந் தலை do share the value of sharing food. But 182 only lists it first, it does not rank it, and the same list holds inner dispositions (முனிவிலர், பிறர் அஞ்சுவது அஞ்சி), so the teaches' 'not an inner disposition' contradicts the poem.

183's சிறப்பின் பாலால் தாயும் மனம் திரியும் among children of one womb and 69's mother who rejoices more than at birth to hear her son called சான்றோன் both make the mother respond to a son's worth. 183 carries it to the harder consequence, favour among siblings, which is a real development and what the teaches says.

Both stage a cry of tiger while girls pluck vengai on the slope: புலிபுலி என்னும் பூசல் (48) and the குறமகள் whose பூசல் is taken for ஆகொள் வயப்புலி (52). The image is distinctive and the contrast holds: in 48 the alarm brings the lover, in 52 it describes the hero's land while the heroine forbids disclosure. 'Known custom' is a modest inference from two poets using it.

Both have a man wanting home at evening (மனைகலந்து மாலை அயர்கம் விருந்து; the drive to reach her by புல்லென் மாலை). That is the shared homecoming situation; 1268 is a wish while the king's war goes on, 234 a return after it. The teaches' 'fixed goal in both traditions' restates the topic.

The image is shared: ஓரில் நெய்தல் கறங்க ஓர்இல் ... முழவின் பாணி (194) and மணப்பறை ... பிணப்பறையாய் (N23). The note names the reading the tension rests on (இனிய காண்க as seeking good within the world against உய்ந்துபோம் ஆறு), which is defensible from 194's Tamil. 'Reusing a Sangam image' as a claim of borrowing is not proven, but the contrast of conclusions holds.

192's வாழ்தல் இனிதென மகிழ்ந்தன்றும் இலமே ... இன்னாதென்றலும் இலமே and 379's question why those who take good as good grieve at ill state the same equanimity. 192 grounds it in the raft that முறைவழிப் படூஉம், which gives the Kural's argument an image; 379 does not itself say ஊழ் (that is its chapter), a small slip in the teaches.

Both Paranar poems use the Kazhar legend: 222's மருதி who showed ஆதி மந்தி her lover and entered the sea, and 236's ஆதி மந்தி asking land after land for ஆட்டன் அத்தி. The friend holds up Maruthi's fame as a goal, the wife likens her own distraction to Manthi's; 'shame' slightly overstates 236's பேதுபெரிது உறல், but the two purposes are rightly drawn.
links.text_issue: 236 line 20 was repaired by splitting; 222 sense flagged as uncertain.

links.reason: 189: செல்வத்துப் பயனே ஈதல்; துய்ப்பேம் எனினே தப்புந பலவே, grounded in உண்பது நாழி உடுப்பவை இரண்டே; N9: the hoarder இழந்தான் என்று எண்ணப்படும். The teaches rightly separates the bodily ground of 189 from the miser's failures in N9; it reads தப்புந பலவே as loss, which is one sense of the line.

Kural 1060 asks the asker not to be angry (இரப்பான் வெகுளாமை வேண்டும்). 196 names the king's fault sharply (இரப்போர் வாட்டல் ... புரப்போர் புகழ்குறை) and then blesses (நோயிலர் ஆகநின் புதல்வர்), with வெயிலென முனியேன். It is a fair reading that rebuke and absence of anger go together, but 'agrees' is loose: 196 adds open blame the Kural's patience does not allow.

43 calls leaving one's companion for wealth மடமை and its doers அளிஇன்று; 53's friend calls the same going அருள், and the heroine replies it is love of பொருள். Different speakers in different situations are not a tension; the sharper link (அளி/அருள் over the same act) goes unmentioned, and 'the woman refuses to call either grace' claims a reply to 43 that 53 does not make.

N206 prefers உப்பிலிப் புற்கை among kin to rich food from அமரார் hands. In 197 the greens and வரகின் சொன்றி are what the small chiefs themselves eat (பெறூஉம் சீறூர் மன்னர்), marking their poverty, not a meal given to the poet; the note misreads this, and 'the patron stands where the family stands' does not follow.

Grey hair is the shared subject: நரையில ஆகுதல் யாங்கு ஆகியர் (191) and நரைவரும் என்றெண்ணி ... குழவியிடத்தே துறந்தார் (N11). One credits the household and the சான்றோர் of one's town, the other counsels leaving the world before age; on the stated reading the two answers do conflict, and the teaches is specific.

Both tell of Cheralathan shamed by the back wound: புறப்புண் நாணி ... வாள் வடக்கு இருந்தனன் (65) and பொருதுபுண் நாணிய சேரலாதன் ... வான்வடக்கிருந்தென (55). 55 alone names the சான்றோர் who went with him to the other world, and uses them for the mother's life that will not follow her daughter, as the teaches says.

The same word sets them against each other: இன்னாது அம்ம இவ்வுலகம் (194) and முனிவின் இன்னாதென்றலும் இலமே (192). As judgments of the world they conflict on the plain reading; the teaches (protest and equanimity side by side in one anthology) is true and specific.

A town likeness for a woman's bangle appears in both: போஒர் அன்ன என் செறிவளை (186) and அள்ளூர் அன்ன என் ஒண்தொடி (46). But in 46 ஒண்தொடி can name the girl herself, likened to Allur, and her bangle slipping (நெகிழினும் நெகிழ்க) is surrender, while 186's unbroken bangle is defiance; the teaches' 'a woman's claim on the man' fits 186, not 46's release.

Uthiyan Cheral's feast is named in both: பெருஞ்சோற்று மிகுபதம் வரையாது கொடுத்தோய் (2) and உதியஞ் சேரல் பெருஞ்சோறு கொடுத்த ஞான்றை இரும்பல் கூளிச் சுற்றம் குழீஇயிருந்தாங்கு (233). The note says what the akam poet does with it, the hills crowding on the track like the கூளி host at the feast, and the teaches follows.

335 urges நல்வினை before the tongue is stopped; 195, also before death (கணிச்சிக் கூர்ம்படை ... பிணிக்கும் காலை), concedes நல்லது செய்தல் ஆற்றீர் ஆயினும் அல்லது செய்தல் ஓம்புமின் and calls that நல்லாற்றுப் படூஉம் நெறி. The added floor is a real qualification and the teaches is accurate.

The wish that he be well while the woman pales is shared (நோய்இலராக நம் காதலர்; பசக்கமன் ... நன்னிலையர் ஆவர் எனின்). The teaches' story that the Kural absorbed the friend's voice into the woman's is speculative, and the colophon of 227 itself allows the heroine as speaker (தலைமகள் சொல்லியதூஉமாம்).

Both size gossip by a public event: ஆர்ப்பினும் பெரிதே after Katti's flight at Uranthai (226) and அலர் ... திங்களைப் பாம்புகொண்டற்று (1146). That is a shared figure, not an agreed claim. The contrast of a historical rout with a cosmic eclipse is real, though 'keeps the old akam habit' is an unproven line of descent.

784's நகுதல் is laughter and 860's நகல் is friendly gladness set against இகல்; they share only a root in two senses. The link also leans on Parimelazhagar's gloss, and neither verse limits the other; the teaches restates the shared word. Kural to Kural, not from a Sangam verse.

475 speaks only of a cart and peacock feathers (பீலிபெய் சாகாடும் அச்சிறும்); the allegory of a king taking on many weak enemies comes entirely from Parimelazhagar, as the marker's own nuance admits. Without the commentary there is no development to 873's தமியனாய்ப் பல்லார் பகைகொள்பவன். Kural to Kural.

Both refuse the promise of a quick return: 1151's நின் வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க்கு உரை and 229's 'இன்னே வருதும்' எனத் தெளித்தோரே ... இன்இள வேனிலும் வாரார், quoted against the friend's comfort. One is a retort before parting, the other proof from the season after, so the pair treats the situation differently, as the teaches says.

The exclamation is shared: உண்டால் அம்ம இவ்வுலகம் and இன்னாது அம்ம இவ்வுலகம். But 'the world exists because of the selfless' and 'the world is harsh' are not opposite claims; 182 can grant 194's harshness. The teaches' 'opposite things' and 'arguing with itself' overstate a shared formula.

The phrasing matches closely: தனக்கென வாழாப் பிறர்க்கு உரியாளன் (54, of Pannan) and தமக்கென முயலா நோன்தாள் பிறர்க்கென முயலுநர் (182). The teaches is true and specific: the ideal stated generally in 182 is a phrase of praise for a named patron in an akam poem.

187 sets aside நாடு காடு அவல் மிசை and makes the land good எவ்வழி நல்லவர் ஆடவர்; 737 lists a land's உறுப்பு (waters, hill, fort). Listing a land's limbs and judging its goodness are different questions, so the tension is thin. The teaches adds that the Purananuru gave its answer 'before' the treatise, which neither text shows.

Pannan of Sirukudi is the same patron: 173 calls him பசிப்பிணி மருத்துவன் with crowds of children carrying rice from his house, 54 names பண்ணன் சிறுகுடிப் படப்பை and calls him தனக்கென வாழாப் பிறர்க்கு உரியாளன். The note says what the akam poet does (his village's gooseberry gives the simile), and the teaches holds.

399 says the learned love learning more seeing that what delights them delights the world; 650 says those who cannot கற்றது உணர விரித்துரை are scentless flowers. The second adds a real condition on how learning reaches the world, which is the teaches' point. Kural to Kural, not from a Sangam verse.

Rain for those who depend on it figures the lover's gift in both (வாழ்வார்க்கு வானம் பயந்தற்றால்; the dawn rain filling the dry tank, பல்லோர் உவந்த உவகை). But in 42 the image is the friend's joy at his coming to wed, in 1192 the measured grace of lovers; rain as love's boon is common. 'The couplet is the compressed form of the scene' is an unproven claim.

Both turn on புணர்வு and on stopping a departure: 1155 asks that his going be prevented (நீங்கின் அரிதால் புணர்வு); in 51 the man refuses wealth that comes only பிரியின். The word is used in two senses (union with her; wealth 'joined' by parting), so the link rests on a pun, though the teaches describes the two senses accurately.

The phrase நீ வெய்யோளொடு and the Kaveri bathing are shared by these two Paranar poems. But the note says both set it at Matthi's Kazhar: in 6 the bathing is at உறந்தை ஆங்கண் காவிரி நீத்தம், and பல்வேல் மத்தி கழாஅர் is the likeness for the wife's lost youth (கழாஅர் அன்ன எம் இளமை). The teaches' two puram comparisons, a rout and a lost youth, holds.

The ranking is the same and in the same terms: கீழ்ப்பால் ஒருவன் கற்பின் மேற்பால் ஒருவனும் அவன்கண் படுமே (183) and மேற்பிறந்தாராயினும் கல்லாதார் கீழ்ப்பிறந்தும் கற்றார் அனைத்திலர் பாடு (409). Both keep மேல்/கீழ் as the scale that learning overturns, as the teaches says; 'already a king's teaching' is a dating claim neither text fixes.

poems.note: The heron leaving the shore for its lone chick mainly empties the grove; any hint for the lovers is too loose to state.
The Marungur market is an open comparison of his departure's clamour.
The crab keeping to its hole is one item in a catalogue that marks the season; it does not clearly imply anything for the lovers.
Aathimanthi and the broken fort are open similes (போல).
No native vehicle or carrier; the raiders roar like tigers by open simile.

iraicchi.act: At midnight the tiger goes out and kills a gaur to feed his mate weak after bearing young.
iraicchi.sense: The beast provides for his mate; the hero who would part from her must do as much, or has he a cure for her?

poems.note: Nalli's kaanthal is an open comparison of her fragrance.
The fisher girl feeding her father is a likeness chain (தொண்டி அன்ன), not a native vehicle.
The north wind's battering is stated as her own suffering, not hidden.
All likenesses are open (அன்ன, அன்னோள); no native vehicle or carrier.
The bamboo bored by the bee only sounds like a flute; mood, not act.

iraicchi.act: The anril on the palm by the house cannot sleep if one of the pair is parted.
iraicchi.sense: She, parted from him, cannot sleep either, and he who no longer comes should know it.

iraicchi.act: The female bird flies through the heat to the bare fig, finds no fruit and droops remembering the days of plenty.
iraicchi.sense: His wife, left alone, remembers their days together and wastes as the bird does.

poems.note: The Musiri siege is an open comparison (உறுநரின்).
Koodal is an open likeness (அன்ன); no native vehicle or carrier.

iraicchi.act: The red dog rests with its starving mate in the shade of the hero-stone.
iraicchi.sense: Even the wild dog stays by its hungry mate on that track, yet he left her for wealth.

poems.note: Lines 6 to 11 run together; that the dog pair is what rests in the stone's shade is the likelier parse.
The forge bellows and the churned-milk foam are open comparisons.
